territorial_scope.description: Directly applicable in all Member States; applies to providers of very large online platforms and search engines designated under DSA Article 33.

evidence.quote: This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.

summary.short: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/436 sets rules for independent audits under DSA Article 37 of very large online platforms and search engines: auditor independence and selection, audited providers' cooperation duties, audit methodologies, risk analysis, and report templates. Binding in all Member States; in force twenty days after OJ publication.
summary.long: Sets rules for the independent audits that Article 37 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (DSA) requires of very large online platforms and very large online search engines. Addressed to audited providers and auditing organisations. Section I defines terms and the audit period (Arts. 2-3). Section II covers selection of auditors, requiring the provider to check independence, conflict-of-interest, expertise and professional-ethics conditions (Art. 4), cooperation and access to data, systems and personnel (Art. 5), and a written agreement annexed to the audit report (Art. 7). Section III sets audit report and audit implementation report templates in Annexes I and II (Art. 6), and audit conclusions of 'positive', 'positive with comments' or 'negative', from which audit opinions are derived (Art. 8). Section IV sets methodology: audit risk analysis (Art. 9), methodologies and tests including for algorithmic systems (Art. 10), evidence quality (Art. 11), sampling (Art. 12), and specific methodologies for DSA Articles 34, 35, 36 and 37 and for codes of conduct and crisis protocols (Arts. 13-17). Binding and directly applicable in all Member States; enters into force on the twentieth day after publication in the Official Journal (Art. 18). The regulation itself sets no penalties.

relations.note: Adopted under the delegated power in Article 37(7) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065; the title states that it supplements that Regulation. Only instrument cited as a relation in the text.

evidence.quote: Having regard to Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 October 2022 on a Single Market For Digital Services and amending Directive 2000/31/EC (Digital Services Act)

notes: Commission Delegated Regulation dated 20 October 2023, published in the Official Journal on 2.2.2024; entry into force on the twentieth day after publication (Art. 18). The text names no firm and designates no authority; audited providers and auditing organisations are described by category, and the Commission, the Digital Service Coordinator and the European Board for Digital Services appear only as recipients of reports or sources of guidance. Article 13(3)(a) contains an incomplete phrase ('drawn up by the audited including'). Article 7(1)(b) uses 'audit organisation' where the rest of the text uses 'auditing organisation'. The text sets no penalties.

‘auditing organisation’ means an individual organisation, a consortium or other combination of organisations, including any sub-contractors, that the audited provider has contracted to perform an independent audit in accordance with Article 37 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065
‘audited service’ means a very large online platform or a very large online search engine designated in accordance with Article 33 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065
‘audited provider’ means the provider of an audited service which is subject to independent audits pursuant to Article 37(1) of that Regulation
‘audited obligation or commitment’ means an obligation or commitment referred to in Article 37(1) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 which forms the subject matter of the audit

‘internal control’ means any measures, including processes and tests, that are designed, implemented and maintained by the audited provider, including its compliance officers and management body, to monitor and ensure the audited provider’s compliance with the audited obligation or commitment

‘materiality threshold’ means the threshold beyond which deviations or misstatements by the audited provider, individually or aggregated, would reasonably affect the audit findings, conclusions and opinions

‘reasonable level of assurance’ means a high but not absolute level of assurance, which allows the auditing organisation to assert in its audit opinion and audit conclusions whether the audited provider complies with the audited obligations or commitments, based on sufficient and appropriate evidence

obligations.summary: The audit must be performed in a manner and duration allowing the auditing organisation to assess compliance with all audited obligations and commitments with reasonable assurance; the audit period must start immediately after the previous audit period and allow timely completion under Art. 37(1) DSA; where no previous audit exists, the period starts four months after the Art. 33(6) notification.

obligations.applies_from: Entry into force: twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 18)

obligations.summary: The audited provider must transmit to the auditing organisation, before any audit procedure, internal control descriptions, benchmarks, risk analyses and information on decision-making structures and algorithmic systems; grant access without undue delay to data, systems, personnel and premises; and make resources available, including where information is held by a third-party contractor.

obligations.summary: The audit report under Art. 37(4) DSA must be established by the auditing organisation without interference from the audited provider, using the Annex I template with detailed and substantiated conclusions.
obligations.applies_from: Entry into force: twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 18)

evidence.quote: The audit report referred to in Article 37(4) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 shall be established by the auditing organisation, without interference from the audited provider.

evidence.quote: Where applicable, the audit implementation report referred to in Article 37(6) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 shall be drawn up in accordance with the template in Annex II.

obligations.summary: The audited provider and the auditing organisation must conclude a written agreement setting out the audited obligations and commitments, the auditing organisation's responsibilities, data access procedures and contact points, the audit timeframe, and a dispute-resolution procedure.
obligations.applies_from: Entry into force: twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 18)

obligations.summary: The Art. 7(1) agreement and any other agreements or engagement letters between the auditing organisation and the audited provider must be annexed to the audit report; changes made to the agreement during the audit must be made explicit in the audit report.

obligations.summary: The audit report must include conclusions per audited obligation or commitment (positive, positive with comments, or negative) and audit opinions on Chapter III and each code of conduct and crisis protocol; recommendations must be specific and state their effect on the materiality threshold; limited-period non-compliance must be documented; and the report must explain any case where reasonable assurance could not be achieved.
obligations.applies_from: Entry into force: twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 18)
obligations.conditional_on: Operational recommendations and limited-period findings apply where they arise; explanation required where reasonable assurance cannot be achieved (Art. 8(2), (7), (8))

obligations.summary: The audit report must include a substantiated audit risk analysis for each audited obligation or commitment, carried out before audit procedures and updated during the audit, covering inherent, control and detection risks.
obligations.applies_from: Entry into force: twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 18)

evidence.quote: The audit report shall include a substantiated audit risk analysis performed by the auditing organisation

obligations.summary: Audits must use appropriate methodologies reducing assessed audit risks to a level allowing reasonable-assurance conclusions; the report must describe audit criteria, materiality thresholds, tests and methodology changes; the audit must include tests and substantive analytical procedures and assess the accuracy of publicly reported information.
obligations.applies_from: Entry into force: twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 18)
obligations.conditional_on: Reasonable doubts trigger adapted methodology and tests (Art. 10(3)-(4))

evidence.quote: audits shall be performed by using appropriate auditing methodologies to reduce the assessed audit risks

obligations.summary: Audit conclusions and opinions must rest on audit evidence that is relevant and sufficient to reduce identified audit risks and reliable under the auditing organisation's professional judgement and scepticism.
obligations.applies_from: Entry into force: twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 18)

obligations.summary: Where audit evidence is based on a sample, sample size and method must be selected for representativeness and to minimise detection risk, and the audit report must justify the choice of sample size and sampling methodology.

obligations.applies_from: Entry into force: twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 18)

obligations.summary: The assessment of compliance with Art. 35 DSA (risk mitigation) must include analysis of how mitigation measures were identified, whether they were applicable, and whether they are reasonable, proportionate and effective, together with the specified internal control and mitigation-measure assessments.
obligations.applies_from: Entry into force: twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 18)

obligations.summary: The assessment of compliance with Art. 36 DSA (crisis response) must include analysis of whether and how the provider performed the required crisis actions, identified measures and parties affected, assessed their effectiveness and proportionality, and provided the required information to the Commission accurately.
obligations.applies_from: Entry into force: twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 18)

evidence.quote: shall include, but not be limited to, an analysis of whether and how the audited provider performed the required actions

obligations.summary: Compliance with Art. 37 DSA and the Regulation is assessed against the audit(s) for the preceding yearly period, with an assessment of Art. 37(2) compliance for the current audit; where the same or a partly overlapping auditing organisation performed the previous audit, the report must explain the steps taken to ensure objectivity.

entities.note: No named firm, facility or public body is listed. Audited providers, auditing organisations and very large online platforms are described by category only.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff in this regulation changes legal treatment. The numbers that appear (annual audit cycle, four months after notification under Art. 3(3), one year under Art. 3(3), three-year retention under Art. 13(1)(d)) are procedural time limits or obligations and are not coded as thresholds. The materiality threshold is defined in Art. 2(12) without a number.

enforcement.note: The text contains no fines, penalties, licence revocation, suspension, blocking or other sanction provisions. It refers to Article 37 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 and sets audit, report and implementation-report requirements, but states no enforcement consequences for non-compliance.
